{{Quote|Choose someone as a successor and you will inevitably be succeeded. Choose someone hungrier and you will be devoured. Choose someone quicker and you won't dodge the blade at your back. Choose someone with more patience and you won't block the blade at your throat. Choose someone more devious and you'll hold the blade that kills you. Choose someone more clever and you'll never know your end. Despite these cautions, an apprentice is essential. A Master without an apprentice is a Master of nothing.|[[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], as [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] of the [[Telos Holocron]]|<ref name="JediVsSith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>}}
'''Sith Master''' was the title of a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] individual who [[Sith training|instructed]] at least one [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] in the ways of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Traditionally, the apprentice was required to [[Death/Legends|kill]] his or her mentor before they could train their own apprentice and advance to the rank of Master.

Throughout Sith history, the Master held the titles [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] and [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]]. In [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan's]] [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]], Sith Masters held the rank of Sith Lord, but only the strongest Master ruled as Dark Lord of the Sith. Under [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane's]] [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]], the guiding principle of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]], the Master and his or her apprentice held both titles together.

The Sith Master's role stood in contrast to the rank of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]], a title given to members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]&mdash;adherents to the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side of the Force]]. Like the Sith Rule of Two, the [[Jedi Code/Legends|Jedi Code]] expressly forbade any master from training two or more apprentices simultaneously.

==History==
{{Quote|Any Master who instructs more than one apprentice in the ways of the dark side is a fool. In time, the apprentices will unite their strength and overthrow the Master. It is inevitable. Axiomatic. That is why each Master must have only one student.|Darth Revan, as [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] of a [[Darth Revan's Sith Holocron|Sith Holocron]]|<ref name="POE">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Order_of_the_Sith_Lord-_BoS.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Sith Master and his apprentice]]
Throughout various incarnations of the [[Sith Order]], the rank of Master was held by [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] adherents to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] who [[Sith training|trained]] one or more [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentices]] in the ways of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]. During the reign of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]], Sith Masters were barred from instructing multiple disciples at the same time&mdash;a decree influenced by Revan's belief that lesser Sith would form an alliance to overthrow their outnumbered Master. As an example of his own policy, Revan trained a single apprentice, [[Darth Malak]], during his tenure as the ruling [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="POE" />

[[1000 BBY/Legends|Roughly three thousand years]] after the [[Jedi Civil War|war]] between the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and Darth Revan's [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]], [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] brought about the [[Death/Legends|deaths]] of thousands of Sith in the final days of the [[New Sith Wars]]. The [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], an order of numerous Sith, had left Bane disillusioned with the way that the organization broke away from Sith traditions. After the entire Brotherhood was destroyed at the [[Seventh Battle of Ruusan]], Bane formed the [[Order of the Sith Lords]]. Guided by the [[Rule of Two/Legends|Rule of Two]], only two Sith Lords were allowed to exist at any given time&mdash;a Master who embodied the power of the dark side; and an apprentice who coveted the power. Bane, who had grown inspired by Revan's views on the relationship between Master and apprentice,<ref name="POE" /> trained only one apprentice as his eventual successor, [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]].<ref name="ROT">''[[Darth Bane: Rule of Two]]''</ref><ref name="DOE">''[[Darth Bane: Dynasty of Evil]]''</ref> Throughout the following millennium, the mantle of Sith Master passed from mentor to apprentice, usually through single combat to the death as Bane had envisioned.<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

The Rule of Two remained in effect during the [[Galactic Standard Calendar|last century]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], although it was no longer strictly adhered to by modern Sith Lords. [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], like several Masters before him, was hesitant to train an apprentice, only to be replaced through eventual betrayal and murder. Plagueis's own Master, [[Darth Tenebrous/Legends|Darth Tenebrous]], had secretly trained another student, [[Darth Venamis]], without his apprentice's knowledge. Plagueis hoped to break the homicidal tradition of the Rule of Two with his apprentice, [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], but was ultimately slain by the ambitious Sith Lord who sought to rule [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]].<ref name="Plagueis" />

[[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious was a master of several apprentices at different points in his life.<ref name="JediVsSith" /> While still learning the ways of the dark side under Plagueis's guidance, Sidious trained a [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]], known as [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], as a [[Sith assassin/Legends|Sith assassin]].<ref name="Plagueis" /> Maul was then followed by two former members of the Jedi Order, [[Dooku/Legends|Darth Tyranus]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] respectively.<ref name="JediVsSith" />

Though Darth Vader never attained the rank of Sith Master, he secretly instructed his own Sith apprentice in a plot to overthrow the Emperor. [[Galen Marek]], a prodigy of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], served the Dark Lord as his personal [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] for [[Standard year/Legends|years]] under the codename "Starkiller."<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref> Marek's redemption as a Jedi and untimely demise forced Vader to [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] his former apprentice in the hopes of creating a stronger and more loyal version of the original Starkiller. Out of the [[Aberrant clone|numerous test subjects]] who failed to meet Vader's expectations, including a [[Subject 1138|renegade clone]],<ref name="TFUIIn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> only [[Dark Apprentice|one clone]] completed his trials and became Darth Vader's new apprentice.<ref name="DT">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'': "Distant Thunder" cutscenes</ref>

The Order of the Sith Lords ended with the demise of the last clone of Emperor Palpatine<ref name="EE2">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref> in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> but the Rule of Two was preserved by a new Sith Master, the self-proclaimed Dark Lady of the Sith [[Lumiya]]. Having received partial Sith instruction under both Sidious and Vader, Lumiya [[Lumiya's Sith|rebuilt]] Bane's Order and instructed two apprentices in turn, the former [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Flint]] and a [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guardsman]] named [[Carnor Jax]].<ref name="end">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Her third and final apprentice, [[Darth Caedus]], achieved Sith Mastery shortly before Lumiya's death in a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|duel]] [[Duel on Terephon|against]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> Caedus anointed the Jedi [[Tahiri Veila]] as his apprentice, and thus continued the Rule of Two until his own death in [[41 ABY]].<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

Even before the collapse of Lumiya's Sith Order,<ref name="Inferno">''[[Legacy of the Force: Inferno]]''</ref> a new policy was established by a Sith Master called [[Darth Krayt]]. The [[Rule of One]] reopened the Sith ranks to more than two Sith Lords, and thus allowed Krayt's [[One Sith|Order]] to expand with more than several hundred members by [[130 ABY]]. The tradition of Master and apprentice remained, but the revived Sith Order was composed of many Masters, each with their own apprentice; and all ultimately answered directly to the one Dark Lord of the Sith.<ref name="Legacy0">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0]]</ref>
